rows.descriptionText:
linkAbout Fuel Cycle:

Fuel Cycle empowers leading organizations with agile research solutions that deliver decision-ready insights — fast, flexible, and fully integrated. As a market research disruptor, our AI-powered Insights Platform is built for speed, precision, and scale. With cutting-edge tools and seamless audience connectivity, we help brands ditch the guesswork and make smarter, customer-led decisions at lightning speed.

Why work at Fuel Cycle?

Join a high-growth team where curiosity is valued, ownership is encouraged, and your work drives real-world impact. Whether you’re based at our Los Angeles HQ, New York City hub, working remotely across the U.S., or part of our global team in India, you’ll help shape the future of decision intelligence for some of the world’s most iconic brands.

The Role:

The AI Operations Associate is Fuel Cycle’s AI transformation role, with one mission: make every function in the company AI-native. We start with IT, Services, Sales, and Marketing.

You’ll begin by owning our AI for IT stack. That means deploying agentic workflows across the Service Desk, application management, and cybersecurity operations. You’ll shape the roadmap alongside our Chief AI Officer, then build and ship it.

This is not an IT Operations seat with AI bolted on. You’ll own the shift from manual, hand-offs-between-people workflows to AI-driven pipelines, and you’ll measure and report the business impact of each one.

If an agent can do the work, you build it. You architect, build, and deploy the replacement. If it can’t yet, you make it possible. You fix the underlying data and re-engineer the process until it can. 

AI for IT is your starting point, and from day one you’ll work in lockstep with Services, Marketing, and Finance. As our internal playbook matures, your scope grows to HR, Legal, Customer Success, and the rest of the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities

IT Operations (Initial focus)

Own the AI-Native Service Desk & App Automation: Architect and deploy autonomous AI agents capable of resolving IT help desk tickets independently. You will move beyond basic ticket triage to build self-executing agentic workflows for software provisioning, account access management, hardware procurement, and system troubleshooting. Ship Autonomous Security & Network Pipelines: Design and deploy end-to-end AI pipelines that automate core cybersecurity operations and infrastructure tasks. This includes agentifying threat detection, anomaly isolation, routine patch management, firewall adjustments, and new user network configurations. Optimize Enterprise IT Metrics via Agent Deployment: Deploy, monitor, and continuously tune agents against strict internal SLAs. You will own the optimization loops to ensure that agentic execution directly improves core IT performance metrics—slashing time-to-resolution, reducing system downtime, and eliminating manual routing bottlenecks. Build the IT Intelligence Layer (BI Dashboards): Design and maintain robust Business Intelligence (BI) dashboards that grant real-time visibility into infrastructure health, agent performance, software utilization, and security vectors. You will transform raw operational logs into a single, trusted source of truth for leadership. Partner with Product Management to Shape the Field: Work in lockstep with the Product and Engineering teams to dogfood internal breakthroughs. You will act as "Customer Zero," feeding your real-world IT operational telemetry and agent design patterns back into Fuel Cycle's core AI platform development lifecycle. 

Broader Internal Operations (Expanding Scope)

Identify and prioritize AI automation opportunities across all internal functions — HR, Legal, Customer Success, IT, and others — as GTM coverage matures. Establish and own the internal AI operations playbook: how Fuel Cycle evaluates, deploys, and measures AI-native replacements for manual workflows company-wide. Champion AI fluency across internal teams — helping department leaders understand what is automatable, what isn't yet, and what the roadmap looks like. Partner with Product & Engineering on the underlying platform and MCP infrastructure that powers internal agent surfaces. 

Systems, Data & Measurement

Own the "single source of truth" standard across all functions you support — ensuring data is clean, definitions are agreed, and escalations over numbers are rare. Instrument every AI workflow you deploy with evaluation loops so quality, accuracy, and reliability are continuously measured. Maintain a clear, quantified view of manual hours displaced, workflow coverage, and time-to-answer improvement — and report it to leadership. 

Your Success Metrics

AI-Native Coverage — Percentage of routine workflows across supported functions executed or materially assisted by AI agents. Manual Hours Displaced — Dollar-equivalent time returned to IT, and other operational leaders each quarter. Speed to Answer — Time from a leader's question to a trustworthy answer, whether via dashboard, agent response, or ad hoc analysis. Data Trust — Reduction in escalations and disputes over pipeline, attribution, revenue, and operational numbers. Function Coverage Expansion — Number of internal functions with at least one AI-native workflow deployed and measured. 

Who You'll Work With

Chief Product and AI OfficerHead of ProductsHead of EngineeringDevOpsCMO and Marketing leadershipCFO and Finance leadershipHR, Legal, and other functional leaders (as scope expands)The existing AI Operations Associate (peer, focused on customer-facing teams)

Core Skills, Competencies & Attributes

Strong systems thinker — able to hold Salesforce architecture, a marketing automation platform, a finance stack, and other internal tooling in view simultaneously and see the seams between them. Fluent in AI-native workflow concepts: agents, MCP, prompt engineering, evaluation loops, and human-in-the-loop design. Comfortable owning the "single source of truth" burden across multiple functions with competing priorities. Communicates clearly with both technical (engineering) and commercial (sales, marketing, finance, operations) audiences. Bias to build and ship — will prototype the replacement rather than document the current state. 

Required Experience & Technical Skills

Track record of building and shipping solutions with AI in a business context. Hands-on experience with agentic development: Claude Code, MCP, prompt engineering, evaluation loops. Python for data analysis and automation; SQL for querying and reporting. Familiarity with enterprise operational systems (CRM, marketing automation, ERP, BI) — enough to build against them, with willingness to become fluent across the stack. Comfort with ambiguity and strong prioritization instincts across a broad operational scope. 

Benefits & Perks:

Fuel Cycle is committed to supporting the well-being, flexibility, and growth of our team. We offer a competitive and inclusive benefits package that includes:

Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance plans401(k) with Company Match: Plan for your future with our retirement savings programEquity Purchase Option: Participate in Fuel Cycle’s long-term successFlexible Work Schedule: Empowering you to balance life and workGenerous Time Off:15 vacation days and 7 sick days per year12 company holidays4 floating holidays/recharge days to rest or celebrate what matters to youPaid Parental Leave: Time to bond with your growing familyMonthly Internet & Phone Stipend: Support for remote work setupWellness & Lifestyle Perks: Access to tools like Rightway (healthcare navigation), Headspace (mental wellness), Peloton (fitness), and moreTeam Connection Perks:Weekly community lunches, refreshments, and snacks at our LA & NY headquarters
Compensation Overview:

The expected starting salary range for this position is $85,000 - $105,000. This range represents the typical starting compensation offered to candidates hired into this role. Final base salary will be determined based on a variety of factors, including location, work experience, skills, knowledge, education, and certifications.

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Equal Opportunity:

We believe that everyone, regardless of their background or identity, should have equal access to opportunities for growth and advancement. Our selection processes and career pathways are designed to be fair, transparent, and free from bias. We value the unique perspectives and contributions of each team member, knowing that this diverse range of experiences strengthens our team. rows.title: Market Research Analyst or Senior Analyst, Technology Practice

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
NRG is a leading global insights and strategy firm at the confluence of content, culture, and technology . We stay ahead of what ’ s next, providing fresh insights to spark new ideas . We ’ re a trusted partner to our clients, working behind the scenes to bring imagination, depth, and clarity to their biggest challenges — in entertainment, technology, lifestyle, sports, and gaming . Together, we create with confidence.

We’re proud of our company’s values – these values guide us as we navigate sunny days, gray skies and everything in between:

 Do what you love. With conviction.  Where discovery lives. And impact drives.  Celebrate difference . Cultivate belonging .  Big thinking. Collectively inspired.  Embrace the journey. Be human. 


 The Opportunity 

NRG is seeking a Research Analyst or Senior Analyst to join our Technology research practice. In this role, you’ll collaborate with some of the world’s most influential brands shaping the future of technology. Our team stays at the forefront of innovation—whether exploring what the next generation of technology might look like, reimagining beloved products, diving deep into the evolving role of AI, and beyond.

In this role, you will support a wide range of initiatives across the full project lifecycle from survey design to report delivery. If you’re passionate about quantitative and qualitative research; if you enjoy visualizing data and discovering insights with confidence; and are looking for a great opportunity to start your career where you can make an impact, this opportunity is for you !

 Your Impact 

 Support all phases of quantitative and qualitative research projects, including research design, questionnaire and discussion guide development, data analysis and storytelling.  Projects may include methods such as concept evaluation, brand studies, content optimization tests, messaging/positioning evaluation, creative materials tests, market sizing and segmentation.  Translate data into clear, actionable insights and recommendations through visual, creative and story-driven reports.  Help drive quality control processes at each step of the research lifecycle, from checking survey programming logic, questionnaire proofing, number checking and proofing reports and presentations for accuracy.  Partner closely with internal teams (programming, fieldwork, data processing, design) to keep projects moving forward on tight timelines.  Leverage AI-enabled approaches to enhance the speed, scale, and depth of insight generation across research and storytelling. 


Who We're Looking For

 Prior Experience – Prior internship or work experience in market research or consumer insights .  Writing and storytelling – You know how to connect the dots and turn complex research findings into clear, compelling narratives. Whether you are writing a report, building a presentation, or presenting to a client, you bring insights to life in a way that captures attention and drives decisions.  Curious and future-minded – You are genuinely interested in seeking information on the “whys,” always digging for more information to understand what makes consumers tick. You’re constantly asking “what’s changing?” and “what’s next?”—especially when it comes to audiences, technology, and content strategy.  Consumer-to-market translator – You’re skilled at moving from consumer insight to strategic implication, helping answer the question: “So what does this mean for our technology clients ?”  Problem Solver – You are a natural problem solver. When something doesn’t go as planned, your first instinct is to look for a solution, rather than viewing it as a roadblock.  Data-driven critical thinker – You’re comfortable working with data to identify trends and insights, including both structured ( i.e. data and hard numbers) and unstructured ( i.e. interviews and qualitative) data. You have experience visualizing data with tools such as Excel and PowerPoint .  Data analysis techniques and software – Familiarity with any of the following data analysis techniques would be ideal: statistical significance testing, correlation analysis, multivariate analysis techniques (such as cluster/segmentation analysis ) and conjoint and discrete choice analysis. Experience with SPSS, Q, or advanced analytics is a plus but not required .  AI-curious and capable – You have experience using AI tools and are thoughtful about how AI can enhance—not replace—insight work.  Self-starter – Internally-motivated who continuously strives to get things done well, regardless of challenges encountered . You are proactive and always keep an eye on the next step.  Clear and proactive communicator – You have excellent verbal communication skills and are able to communicate clearly and succinctly. You’re comfortable asking questions and sharing your point of view.  Hawk-eyed attention to detail – You notice when font sizes change unexpectedly or a proper noun isn’t capitalized. Errors don’t get past you and you are always focused on ensuring high levels of quality control and reporting.  Great team member – T eam player who works collaboratively and harmoniously within a team and across teams. You welcome feedback because you have a zest for learning and growing.  Your degree(s) – You have a B.A./B.S. degree in areas such as Social Sciences, Psychology, Business, Marketing, Market Research, Statistics, Economics or a r elated field. Additional degrees are welcome! 


 Position Type 

This is a full-time, exempt position.

What We Offer

We embrace the current era of work and what it means to be a best-in-class employer. We understand the flexibility that is required to recruit and retain incredible talent, whether it’s empowering you to do your best work from the comfort of your home or supporting you if you need to take a mental health day for self-care and rest. Below is a unique blend of benefits tailored to meeting the ever-changing professional landscape.

 Flexible/Remote work with optional usage of our great offices in Culver City or New York  Unlimited PTO, volunteer days and a generous number of recharge days including a full office closure during the week of Christmas and New Year’s  Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance Plans  401K with company match  Generous paid Parental Leave  Regular performance evaluations with opportunities for promotions and merit increases  Educational and training reimbursement plan and other training and professional development opportunities  Employee perks program (includes discounts on travel, hotels, cars, fitness, movie tickets and more)  Resources available for mental health, inclusive care and family building  NRGratitude – our company-wide employee recognition program  Regular team/company events and activities including annual summer and holiday parties  Pet friendly headquarters and pet insurance options 


 Our Commitment 

Diversity, equity, and inclusion is at the center of all our practices to ensure that NRG is a place where people from all identities and backgrounds can thrive. NRG is committed to recruiting and retaining diverse talent by supporting their growth through learning programs, internal mobility, affinity group participation and leadership development. Our differences make us a stronger workforce and enhance our creativity and innovation. We are proud to be an inclusive workplace for all and are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by state, federal, or local law.

Compensation

In order to comply with equal pay and salary transparency laws in various locations, we believe the target range of base compensation in all locations within the United States for this role is $62,000 -$7 8 , 0 00. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and location.

rows.title: AI Operations Associate
rows.descriptionText:
LinkAbout Fuel Cycle

Fuel Cycle empowers leading organizations with agile research solutions that deliver decision-ready insights — fast, flexible, and fully integrated. As a market research disruptor, our AI-powered Insights Platform is built for speed, precision, and scale. With cutting-edge tools and seamless audience connectivity, we help brands ditch the guesswork and make smarter, customer-led decisions at lightning speed.

Why work at Fuel Cycle?

Join a high-growth team where curiosity is valued, ownership is encouraged, and your work drives real-world impact. Whether you’re based at our Los Angeles HQ, New York City hub, working remotely across the U.S., or part of our global team in India, you’ll help shape the future of decision intelligence for some of the world’s most iconic brands.

The Role

The AI Operations Associate is Fuel Cycle’s AI transformation role, with one mission: make every function in the company AI-native. We start with IT, Services, Sales, and Marketing.

You’ll begin by owning our AI for IT stack. That means deploying agentic workflows across the Service Desk, application management, and cybersecurity operations. You’ll shape the roadmap alongside our Chief AI Officer, then build and ship it.

This is not an IT Operations seat with AI bolted on. You’ll own the shift from manual, hand-offs-between-people workflows to AI-driven pipelines, and you’ll measure and report the business impact of each one.

If an agent can do the work, you build it. You architect, build, and deploy the replacement.If it can’t yet, you make it possible. You fix the underlying data and re-engineer the process until it can.

AI for IT is your starting point, and from day one you’ll work in lockstep with Services, Marketing, and Finance. As our internal playbook matures, your scope grows to HR, Legal, Customer Success, and the rest of the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities

IT Operations (Initial focus)

Own the AI-Native Service Desk & App Automation: Architect and deploy autonomous AI agents capable of resolving IT help desk tickets independently. You will move beyond basic ticket triage to build self-executing agentic workflows for software provisioning, account access management, hardware procurement, and system troubleshooting.Ship Autonomous Security & Network Pipelines: Design and deploy end-to-end AI pipelines that automate core cybersecurity operations and infrastructure tasks. This includes agentifying threat detection, anomaly isolation, routine patch management, firewall adjustments, and new user network configurations.Optimize Enterprise IT Metrics via Agent Deployment: Deploy, monitor, and continuously tune agents against strict internal SLAs. You will own the optimization loops to ensure that agentic execution directly improves core IT performance metrics—slashing time-to-resolution, reducing system downtime, and eliminating manual routing bottlenecks.Build the IT Intelligence Layer (BI Dashboards): Design and maintain robust Business Intelligence (BI) dashboards that grant real-time visibility into infrastructure health, agent performance, software utilization, and security vectors. You will transform raw operational logs into a single, trusted source of truth for leadership.Partner with Product Management to Shape the Field: Work in lockstep with the Product and Engineering teams to dogfood internal breakthroughs. You will act as "Customer Zero," feeding your real-world IT operational telemetry and agent design patterns back into Fuel Cycle's core AI platform development lifecycle.

Broader Internal Operations (Expanding Scope)

Identify and prioritize AI automation opportunities across all internal functions — HR, Legal, Customer Success, IT, and others — as GTM coverage matures.Establish and own the internal AI operations playbook: how Fuel Cycle evaluates, deploys, and measures AI-native replacements for manual workflows company-wide.Champion AI fluency across internal teams — helping department leaders understand what is automatable, what isn't yet, and what the roadmap looks like.Partner with Product & Engineering on the underlying platform and MCP infrastructure that powers internal agent surfaces.

Systems, Data & Measurement

Own the "single source of truth" standard across all functions you support — ensuring data is clean, definitions are agreed, and escalations over numbers are rare.Instrument every AI workflow you deploy with evaluation loops so quality, accuracy, and reliability are continuously measured.Maintain a clear, quantified view of manual hours displaced, workflow coverage, and time-to-answer improvement — and report it to leadership.

Your Success Metrics

AI-Native Coverage — Percentage of routine workflows across supported functions executed or materially assisted by AI agents.Manual Hours Displaced — Dollar-equivalent time returned to IT, and other operational leaders each quarter.Speed to Answer — Time from a leader's question to a trustworthy answer, whether via dashboard, agent response, or ad hoc analysis.Data Trust — Reduction in escalations and disputes over pipeline, attribution, revenue, and operational numbers.Function Coverage Expansion — Number of internal functions with at least one AI-native workflow deployed and measured.

Who You'll Work With

Chief Product and AI OfficerHead of ProductsHead of EngineeringDevOpsCMO and Marketing leadershipCFO and Finance leadershipHR, Legal, and other functional leaders (as scope expands)The existing AI Operations Associate (peer, focused on customer-facing teams)

Core Skills, Competencies & Attributes

Strong systems thinker — able to hold Salesforce architecture, a marketing automation platform, a finance stack, and other internal tooling in view simultaneously and see the seams between them.Fluent in AI-native workflow concepts: agents, MCP, prompt engineering, evaluation loops, and human-in-the-loop design.Comfortable owning the "single source of truth" burden across multiple functions with competing priorities.Communicates clearly with both technical (engineering) and commercial (sales, marketing, finance, operations) audiences.Bias to build and ship — will prototype the replacement rather than document the current state.

Required Experience & Technical Skills

Track record of building and shipping solutions with AI in a business context.Hands-on experience with agentic development: Claude Code, MCP, prompt engineering, evaluation loops.Python for data analysis and automation; SQL for querying and reporting.Familiarity with enterprise operational systems (CRM, marketing automation, ERP, BI) — enough to build against them, with willingness to become fluent across the stack.Comfort with ambiguity and strong prioritization instincts across a broad operational scope.

Benefits & Perks

Fuel Cycle is committed to supporting the well-being, flexibility, and growth of our team. We offer a competitive and inclusive benefits package that includes:

Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance plans401(k) with Company Match: Plan for your future with our retirement savings programEquity Purchase Option: Participate in Fuel Cycle’s long-term successFlexible Work Schedule: Empowering you to balance life and workGenerous Time Off:15 vacation days and 7 sick days per year12 company holidays4 floating holidays/recharge days to rest or celebrate what matters to youPaid Parental Leave: Time to bond with your growing familyMonthly Internet & Phone Stipend: Support for remote work setupWellness & Lifestyle Perks: Access to tools like Rightway (healthcare navigation), Headspace (mental wellness), Peloton (fitness), and moreTeam Connection Perks:Weekly community lunches, refreshments, and snacks at our LA & NY headquarters
Compensation Overview

The expected starting salary range for this position is $85,000 - $105,000. This range represents the typical starting compensation offered to candidates hired into this role. Final base salary will be determined based on a variety of factors, including location, work experience, skills, knowledge, education, and certifications.

Commitment To Diversity, Equity, And Equal Opportunity

At Fuel Cycle, we embrace the values of diversity, equity, and inclusion and are committed to fostering an inclusive company culture. We believe that everyone, regardless of their background or identity, should have equal access to opportunities for growth and advancement. Our selection processes and career pathways are designed to be fair, transparent, and free from bias. We value the unique perspectives and contributions of each team member, knowing that this diverse range of experiences strengthens our team. Fuel Cycle stands firmly against discrimination based on disability, sex, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, veteran status, or any other protected status under the law.

Fuel Cycle is an equal opportunity employer and fully comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). We will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants and employees with disabilities, as needed, to enable them to perform the essential functions of their job and participate in the application and interview process. If you require accommodations during any part of the application process, please contact us at hr@fuelcycle.com to discuss your needs.

rows.title: Pricing Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About We Sell Cellular
We Sell Cellular (WSC) is a leading provider in the secondary mobile device industry, specializing in the sourcing, processing, and distribution of pre-owned mobile devices. Through our operations, technology, and industry expertise, we help extend the lifecycle of mobile devices and support a more accessible and sustainable global device ecosystem.
WSC is part of the ITOCHU Group, providing the strength and resources of a global organization while maintaining an entrepreneurial and collaborative working environment. Our team is focused on operational excellence, continued growth, and building a business that delivers long-term value for our customers, employees, and partners.
Position Summary
We Sell Cellular buys used and refurbished mobile devices in volume from carriers, OEM programs, and trade-in channels, and resells them through wholesale and retail channels. Every purchase begins with a bid, and every bid is a pricing judgment: what the device will sell for, what it will cost to grade and refurbish, and what margin remains. This is a developing analytical role designed for an early-career professional who will build expertise in device pricing, purchasing, grading, refurbishment economics, and secondary-market dynamics. The Pricing Analyst will initially work closely with experienced Buyers and the Director of Sourcing and will take on greater ownership of pricing analysis and recommendations as their market knowledge and judgment develop.
This role reports to the Director of Sourcing and supports Buyers and cross-functional teams across Sales, Operations, Finance, and Engineering/Data by analyzing pricing, demand, product condition, and cost data to inform purchasing decisions, monitor margins, and improve pricing accuracy and reporting.
Key Responsibilities
Price Analysis (Purchasing)Market price tracking. Maintain a current view of buy-side and sell-side prices by model, storage, carrier, and grade: daily award prices, secondary-market and wholesale prices, and WSC's own realized sale pricesComparable analysis. Build like-for-like comparisons across sources and time so that a bid can be judged against what the same device actually cost and sold for recentlyMargin visibility. Track the spread between purchase price and realized sale price by category, including grading and refurbishment cost, and flag categories where margin is compressingData hygiene. Keep pricing data sets clean and consistent; flag data quality issues to Engineering / Data rather than working around them
Bid Price Decision SupportBid analysis support. Prepare analysis for lot and program bids, including expected resale value, margin, grade mix, and other key assumptions. Develop pricing recommendations in partnership with Buyers and the Director of Sourcing, taking on greater ownership as market knowledge and experience develop.Scenario analysis. Show how the recommendation changes under different resale prices, grade mixes, or demand conditions, so the Buyer can decide how aggressive to bePricing floor support. Maintain and prepare the data and analysis used by the Director of Sourcing and Buyers to establish and review pricing floors; monitor bids against established parameters and flag exceptions.Post-bid review. Compare bid assumptions with actual outcomes including realized price, grade mix and sell-through and feed the learning back into the next recommendation
Reporting & CommunicationDaily and weekly reporting. Contribute to the daily market report and weekly purchasing KPI review with price movements, margin trends, and notable bidsDocumentation. Record pricing decisions, assumptions, and outcomes so that the team's pricing knowledge accumulates rather than living in individual headsBuyer partnership. Work closely with Buyers on live bids to understand the information needed for purchasing decisions, respond quickly to analytical requests, and progressively build knowledge of WSC's bidding and purchasing process.
QualificationsMust-haveBachelor's degree in business, economics, finance, statistics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experienceStrong numerical judgment and comfort working with prices, margins, and volumes in spreadsheetsAdvanced spreadsheet skills (Google Sheets / Excel): lookups, pivots, scenario tablesClear written communication — able to turn analysis into a one-page recommendation with assumptions and risksMarket curiosity — genuine interest in mobile devices, secondary markets, and how prices moveAttention to detail and ownership of the accuracy of every number handed to a Buyer
PreferredInternship or early-career experience in pricing, purchasing, procurement, finance, merchandising, inventory, supply chain, business analytics, or a related area. Relevant internships, academic projects or equivalent practical experience will be considered. Familiarity with carrier and OEM trade-in programs, device grading, or refurbishment economicsExperience building dashboards or automated reports (Looker Studio, Sheets, or similar)Bilingual (Japanese or Spanish) a plus
Key CompetenciesNumerical judgment — knows when a number looks wrong and checks itDecision support mindset — every analysis ends in a recommendation a Buyer can act onAI adoption — Quick to leverage AI to work faster, with the discipline to double-check all dataMarket awareness — follows device launches, carrier moves, and secondary-market prices as a habitDocumentation discipline — assumptions and outcomes recorded so the team learnsCollaboration — works at the Buyer's pace and in the Buyer's languageLearning orientation — builds device, grading, and market knowledge steadily toward the Buyer track
Working ConditionsThis role is based in Edgewood, NY and requires regular on-site presence to work closely with the Purchasing team and Operations / Grading floor.
Salary & BenefitsCompensation: Base Salary Range: $55,000 - $60,000 annually. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, technical skills, and other job-related factors.Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including medical insurance, a 401(k)-retirement plan with company match, paid time off (PTO), and paid company holidays.

rows.descriptionText:
The Transportation Planning and Management Division (TPM) is responsible for the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods on the City's streets, supporting the larger goals of economic and social vitality for people living, working, and doing business in New York City. The Division’s responsibilities include planning, street design, technical analysis, signs, transit development, freight mobility and markings, ensuring the safety of motor vehicle occupants, pedestrians, and cyclists.

The Office of Curb Management within the Division of Transportation Planning & Management is responsible for curb policies across the city’s 6,300 miles of streets and roughly 3 million curbside parking spaces, with a focus on improving safety, reducing double parking and better managing competing demands from loading zones and deliveries to charging infrastructure and waste containerization to support safer, more efficient streets across the city

The Office of Curb Management is seeking a candidate to fill the role of Parking Data Analyst within that unit. In this role, the selected candidate will be charged with developing and implementing a citywide data collection program to examine curbside activity metrics in select neighborhoods throughout the city.

As Parking Data Analyst, the candidate will be responsible for all steps for the citywide data collection program including:

 Data collection planning

The candidate will work with the DOT Parking Planning and Policy team to develop the data collection plan including the neighborhoods that will be covered in the program, the metrics to collect, the methodology, and any consultant work and contracting that may be involved.

 Data collection

The candidate will be responsible for overseeing the actual data collection over the course of the year and managing the consultant relationship. The collection methodology will likely include data collection through timelapse cameras, manual occupancy counts, and/or license plate surveys across ten to twelve neighborhoods in New York City.

 Data processing

The candidate will be responsible for overseeing the processing of the data to ensure the capture of appropriate metrics. This may include overseeing consultant processing of timelapse photos, overseeing spreadsheet/data analysis in Microsoft Excel and similar databases, and ensuring collected data is clean and mappable.

 Data reporting

The candidate will be responsible for writing periodic reports on the status of the data collection effort including annual reports. This will include interpreting the data collection to communicate to a both a technical and general audience, writing reports, generating charts, creating maps, and presenting to DOT leadership.

The candidate should have a solid foundation of experience in transportation planning and data collection of parking and transportation metrics. The candidate should be comfortable with and proficient in creating reports and presentations that distill complex information for both technical and non-technical audiences. The candidate should have strong experience using data analysis tools like Microsoft Excel, R, and ArcGIS. The Analyst will have latitude for independent judgement and will be relied upon to keep the Data Collection program on track, organized, and efficient. The successful candidate will also participate in the general strategic planning/problem-solving sessions and assist in the development and deployment of new technologies, programs, processes, and other strategies. The candidate may also be asked to support special initiatives, projects and other duties assigned to the Unit.

 A doctorate degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and one year of full-time experience in a responsible supervisory, administrative or research capacity in the appropriate field of specialization; or A master's degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and three years of responsible full-time research experience in the appropriate field of specialization; or Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above. parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
linkAbout Fuel Cycle:

Fuel Cycle empowers leading organizations with agile research solutions that deliver decision-ready insights — fast, flexible, and fully integrated. As a market research disruptor, our AI-powered Insights Platform is built for speed, precision, and scale. With cutting-edge tools and seamless audience connectivity, we help brands ditch the guesswork and make smarter, customer-led decisions at lightning speed.

Why work at Fuel Cycle?

Join a high-growth team where curiosity is valued, ownership is encouraged, and your work drives real-world impact. Whether you’re based at our Los Angeles HQ, New York City hub, working remotely across the U.S., or part of our global team in India, you’ll help shape the future of decision intelligence for some of the world’s most iconic brands.

The Role:

The AI Operations Associate is Fuel Cycle’s AI transformation role, with one mission: make every function in the company AI-native. We start with IT, Services, Sales, and Marketing.

You’ll begin by owning our AI for IT stack. That means deploying agentic workflows across the Service Desk, application management, and cybersecurity operations. You’ll shape the roadmap alongside our Chief AI Officer, then build and ship it.

This is not an IT Operations seat with AI bolted on. You’ll own the shift from manual, hand-offs-between-people workflows to AI-driven pipelines, and you’ll measure and report the business impact of each one.

If an agent can do the work, you build it. You architect, build, and deploy the replacement. If it can’t yet, you make it possible. You fix the underlying data and re-engineer the process until it can. 

AI for IT is your starting point, and from day one you’ll work in lockstep with Services, Marketing, and Finance. As our internal playbook matures, your scope grows to HR, Legal, Customer Success, and the rest of the enterprise.

Key Responsibilities

IT Operations (Initial focus)

Own the AI-Native Service Desk & App Automation: Architect and deploy autonomous AI agents capable of resolving IT help desk tickets independently. You will move beyond basic ticket triage to build self-executing agentic workflows for software provisioning, account access management, hardware procurement, and system troubleshooting. Ship Autonomous Security & Network Pipelines: Design and deploy end-to-end AI pipelines that automate core cybersecurity operations and infrastructure tasks. This includes agentifying threat detection, anomaly isolation, routine patch management, firewall adjustments, and new user network configurations. Optimize Enterprise IT Metrics via Agent Deployment: Deploy, monitor, and continuously tune agents against strict internal SLAs. You will own the optimization loops to ensure that agentic execution directly improves core IT performance metrics—slashing time-to-resolution, reducing system downtime, and eliminating manual routing bottlenecks. Build the IT Intelligence Layer (BI Dashboards): Design and maintain robust Business Intelligence (BI) dashboards that grant real-time visibility into infrastructure health, agent performance, software utilization, and security vectors. You will transform raw operational logs into a single, trusted source of truth for leadership. Partner with Product Management to Shape the Field: Work in lockstep with the Product and Engineering teams to dogfood internal breakthroughs. You will act as "Customer Zero," feeding your real-world IT operational telemetry and agent design patterns back into Fuel Cycle's core AI platform development lifecycle. 

Broader Internal Operations (Expanding Scope)

Identify and prioritize AI automation opportunities across all internal functions — HR, Legal, Customer Success, IT, and others — as GTM coverage matures. Establish and own the internal AI operations playbook: how Fuel Cycle evaluates, deploys, and measures AI-native replacements for manual workflows company-wide. Champion AI fluency across internal teams — helping department leaders understand what is automatable, what isn't yet, and what the roadmap looks like. Partner with Product & Engineering on the underlying platform and MCP infrastructure that powers internal agent surfaces. 

Systems, Data & Measurement

Own the "single source of truth" standard across all functions you support — ensuring data is clean, definitions are agreed, and escalations over numbers are rare. Instrument every AI workflow you deploy with evaluation loops so quality, accuracy, and reliability are continuously measured. Maintain a clear, quantified view of manual hours displaced, workflow coverage, and time-to-answer improvement — and report it to leadership. 

Your Success Metrics

AI-Native Coverage — Percentage of routine workflows across supported functions executed or materially assisted by AI agents. Manual Hours Displaced — Dollar-equivalent time returned to IT, and other operational leaders each quarter. Speed to Answer — Time from a leader's question to a trustworthy answer, whether via dashboard, agent response, or ad hoc analysis. Data Trust — Reduction in escalations and disputes over pipeline, attribution, revenue, and operational numbers. Function Coverage Expansion — Number of internal functions with at least one AI-native workflow deployed and measured. 

Who You'll Work With

Chief Product and AI OfficerHead of ProductsHead of EngineeringDevOpsCMO and Marketing leadershipCFO and Finance leadershipHR, Legal, and other functional leaders (as scope expands)The existing AI Operations Associate (peer, focused on customer-facing teams)

Core Skills, Competencies & Attributes

Strong systems thinker — able to hold Salesforce architecture, a marketing automation platform, a finance stack, and other internal tooling in view simultaneously and see the seams between them. Fluent in AI-native workflow concepts: agents, MCP, prompt engineering, evaluation loops, and human-in-the-loop design. Comfortable owning the "single source of truth" burden across multiple functions with competing priorities. Communicates clearly with both technical (engineering) and commercial (sales, marketing, finance, operations) audiences. Bias to build and ship — will prototype the replacement rather than document the current state. 

Required Experience & Technical Skills

Track record of building and shipping solutions with AI in a business context. Hands-on experience with agentic development: Claude Code, MCP, prompt engineering, evaluation loops. Python for data analysis and automation; SQL for querying and reporting. Familiarity with enterprise operational systems (CRM, marketing automation, ERP, BI) — enough to build against them, with willingness to become fluent across the stack. Comfort with ambiguity and strong prioritization instincts across a broad operational scope. 

Benefits & Perks:

Fuel Cycle is committed to supporting the well-being, flexibility, and growth of our team. We offer a competitive and inclusive benefits package that includes:

Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance plans401(k) with Company Match: Plan for your future with our retirement savings programEquity Purchase Option: Participate in Fuel Cycle’s long-term successFlexible Work Schedule: Empowering you to balance life and workGenerous Time Off:15 vacation days and 7 sick days per year12 company holidays4 floating holidays/recharge days to rest or celebrate what matters to youPaid Parental Leave: Time to bond with your growing familyMonthly Internet & Phone Stipend: Support for remote work setupWellness & Lifestyle Perks: Access to tools like Rightway (healthcare navigation), Headspace (mental wellness), Peloton (fitness), and moreTeam Connection Perks:Weekly community lunches, refreshments, and snacks at our LA & NY headquarters
Compensation Overview:

The expected starting salary range for this position is $85,000 - $105,000. This range represents the typical starting compensation offered to candidates hired into this role. Final base salary will be determined based on a variety of factors, including location, work experience, skills, knowledge, education, and certifications.

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Equal Opportunity:

At Fuel Cycle, we embrace the values of diversity, equity, and inclusion and are committed to fostering an inclusive company culture. We believe that everyone, regardless of their background or identity, should have equal access to opportunities for growth and advancement. Our selection processes and career pathways are designed to be fair, transparent, and free from bias. We value the unique perspectives and contributions of each team member, knowing that this diverse range of experiences strengthens our team. Fuel Cycle stands firmly against discrimination based on disability, sex, race, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, veteran status, or any other protected status under the law.

We will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants and employees with disabilities, as needed, to enable them to perform the essential functions of their job and participate in the application and interview process. Responsibilities

Analyze portfolio performance, budget, forecast, resource, delivery, schedule, quality, and risk information to identify trends, insights, and areas for follow up. Create and maintain dashboards, reports, key performance indicators, recurring analytics outputs, and leadership ready summaries for technology stakeholders. Develop financial models, cost views, forecast summaries, scenario analyses, and variance insights that support technology portfolio and project decision making. Partner with technology, finance, product, project, and business teams to understand reporting needs and translate them into accurate analytical outputs. Support Software Development Lifecycle and Agile delivery reporting by analyzing delivery metrics, progress data, dependencies, and execution patterns. Prepare presentations, narratives, and stakeholder updates that communicate data backed insights to technical and non technical audiences. Use Agentic AI, reporting, data analytics, and productivity tools to support research, summarization, analysis, workflow efficiency, and human validated outputs. 

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications 

Must have earned a Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Information Technology, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Economics, or another relevant field before the full time start date.Students must have a graduation date between December 2026 and June 2027. Interest or experience in data analytics, financial management, portfolio reporting, technology delivery, business intelligence, or data informed decision making. Awareness of Software Development Lifecycle and Agile methodology concepts within a technology delivery environment. Foundational understanding of Generative AI concepts, responsible use, appropriate use contexts, prompt based workflows, and human validation of AI generated outputs. Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, communication, organization, problem solving, and collaboration skills. 

Preferred Qualifications

Coursework, projects, internships, student organizations, or extracurricular experience related to data analytics, finance, business analysis, reporting, portfolio management, or technology delivery. Experience using analytical, reporting, or presentation tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, SQL, Python, Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms. Curiosity about Agentic AI reporting, AI enabled analytics, productivity tools, automated insight generation, and responsible validation of AI generated recommendations.  Do what you love. With conviction.  Where discovery lives. And impact drives.  Celebrate difference . Cultivate belonging .  Big thinking. Collectively inspired.  Embrace the journey. Be human. 


 The Opportunity 

NRG is seeking a Research Analyst or Senior Analyst to join our Technology research practice. In this role, you’ll collaborate with some of the world’s most influential brands shaping the future of technology. Our team stays at the forefront of innovation—whether exploring what the next generation of technology might look like, reimagining beloved products, diving deep into the evolving role of AI, and beyond.

In this role, you will support a wide range of initiatives across the full project lifecycle from survey design to report delivery. If you’re passionate about quantitative and qualitative research; if you enjoy visualizing data and discovering insights with confidence; and are looking for a great opportunity to start your career where you can make an impact, this opportunity is for you !

 Your Impact 

 Support all phases of quantitative and qualitative research projects, including research design, questionnaire and discussion guide development, data analysis and storytelling.  Projects may include methods such as concept evaluation, brand studies, content optimization tests, messaging/positioning evaluation, creative materials tests, market sizing and segmentation.  Translate data into clear, actionable insights and recommendations through visual, creative and story-driven reports.  Help drive quality control processes at each step of the research lifecycle, from checking survey programming logic, questionnaire proofing, number checking and proofing reports and presentations for accuracy.  Partner closely with internal teams (programming, fieldwork, data processing, design) to keep projects moving forward on tight timelines.  Leverage AI-enabled approaches to enhance the speed, scale, and depth of insight generation across research and storytelling. 


Who We're Looking For

 Prior Experience – Prior internship or work experience in market research or consumer insights .  Writing and storytelling – You know how to connect the dots and turn complex research findings into clear, compelling narratives. Whether you are writing a report, building a presentation, or presenting to a client, you bring insights to life in a way that captures attention and drives decisions.  Curious and future-minded – You are genuinely interested in seeking information on the “whys,” always digging for more information to understand what makes consumers tick. You’re constantly asking “what’s changing?” and “what’s next?”—especially when it comes to audiences, technology, and content strategy.  Consumer-to-market translator – You’re skilled at moving from consumer insight to strategic implication, helping answer the question: “So what does this mean for our technology clients ?”  Problem Solver – You are a natural problem solver. When something doesn’t go as planned, your first instinct is to look for a solution, rather than viewing it as a roadblock.  Data-driven critical thinker – You’re comfortable working with data to identify trends and insights, including both structured ( i.e. data and hard numbers) and unstructured ( i.e. interviews and qualitative) data. You have experience visualizing data with tools such as Excel and PowerPoint .  Data analysis techniques and software – Familiarity with any of the following data analysis techniques would be ideal: statistical significance testing, correlation analysis, multivariate analysis techniques (such as cluster/segmentation analysis ) and conjoint and discrete choice analysis. Experience with SPSS, Q, or advanced analytics is a plus but not required .  AI-curious and capable – You have experience using AI tools and are thoughtful about how AI can enhance—not replace—insight work.  Self-starter – Internally-motivated who continuously strives to get things done well, regardless of challenges encountered . You are proactive and always keep an eye on the next step.  Clear and proactive communicator – You have excellent verbal communication skills and are able to communicate clearly and succinctly. You’re comfortable asking questions and sharing your point of view.  Hawk-eyed attention to detail – You notice when font sizes change unexpectedly or a proper noun isn’t capitalized. Errors don’t get past you and you are always focused on ensuring high levels of quality control and reporting.  Great team member – T eam player who works collaboratively and harmoniously within a team and across teams. You welcome feedback because you have a zest for learning and growing.  Your degree(s) – You have a B.A./B.S. degree in areas such as Social Sciences, Psychology, Business, Marketing, Market Research, Statistics, Economics or a r elated field. Additional degrees are welcome! 


 Position Type 

This is a full-time, exempt position.

What We Offer

We embrace the current era of work and what it means to be a best-in-class employer. We understand the flexibility that is required to recruit and retain incredible talent, whether it’s empowering you to do your best work from the comfort of your home or supporting you if you need to take a mental health day for self-care and rest. Below is a unique blend of benefits tailored to meeting the ever-changing professional landscape.

 Flexible/Remote work with optional usage of our great offices in Culver City or New York  Unlimited PTO, volunteer days and a generous number of recharge days including a full office closure during the week of Christmas and New Year’s  Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance Plans  401K with company match  Generous paid Parental Leave  Regular performance evaluations with opportunities for promotions and merit increases  Educational and training reimbursement plan and other training and professional development opportunities  Employee perks program (includes discounts on travel, hotels, cars, fitness, movie tickets and more)  Resources available for mental health, inclusive care and family building  NRGratitude – our company-wide employee recognition program  Regular team/company events and activities including annual summer and holiday parties  Pet friendly headquarters and pet insurance options 


 Our Commitment 

Diversity, equity, and inclusion is at the center of all our practices to ensure that NRG is a place where people from all identities and backgrounds can thrive. NRG is committed to recruiting and retaining diverse talent by supporting their growth through learning programs, internal mobility, affinity group participation and leadership development. Our differences make us a stronger workforce and enhance our creativity and innovation. Mastercard's Community Institutions team is launching Team Catalyst, an innovative new account management model designed to redefine how we partner with our longer-tail customers.

As customer expectations evolve and operational complexity increases, we are transforming from a traditional one-to-one account management structure to an agile, team-based model that enables us to deliver deeper expertise, greater consistency, and broader access to Mastercard's capabilities.

Team Catalyst is an incubation team focused on building the future of customer partnership and engagement. We are challenging conventional approaches, creating scalable strategies, leveraging data and automation, and finding new ways to bring the full power of Mastercard to our customers.

This role offers a unique opportunity to help design, build, and scale a new model while directly influencing customer growth, experience, and operational excellence across a portfolio of Community Institution customers.

The Role

As an Analyst, Account Management on Team Catalyst, you will manage a portfolio of Community Institution customers and help deliver an exceptional Mastercard experience.

You will build customer relationships, identify opportunities for growth, support business initiatives, and partner across Mastercard to address customer needs. Working within a highly collaborative team environment, you will help customers maximize the value of their Mastercard partnership while contributing to Team Catalyst's innovative account management model.

Manage: Serve as the primary relationship manager for a portfolio of Community Institution customers, building trusted partnerships and supporting customer success.

Grow: Identify opportunities to expand customer engagement and adoption of Mastercard products, services, and solutions.

Advise: Develop an understanding of customer priorities, challenges, and goals to provide relevant recommendations and support.

Collaborate: Partner with teams across Product, Services, Technology, Operations, Marketing, and Sales to deliver solutions and address customer needs.

Support: Assist with renewals, pricing requests, presentations, business cases, and other commercial activities.

Improve: Contribute ideas and process improvements that enhance customer experience, operational efficiency, and team performance.

 Relationship builder with a passion for customer success. Strong communicator who can build credibility with customers and internal stakeholders. Curious and proactive problem solver. Organized and able to manage multiple priorities effectively. Analytical mindset with the ability to turn insights into action. Collaborative team player who thrives in a fast-paced environment. Growth-oriented with a willingness to learn and take on new challenges. Adaptable, resourceful, and comfortable navigating change.


Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. rows.descriptionText:
NRG is a leading global insights and strategy firm at the confluence of content, culture, and technology . We stay ahead of what ’ s next, providing fresh insights to spark new ideas . We ’ re a trusted partner to our clients, working behind the scenes to bring imagination, depth, and clarity to their biggest challenges — in entertainment, technology, lifestyle, sports, and gaming . Together, we create with confidence.

We’re proud of our company’s values – these values guide us as we navigate sunny days, gray skies and everything in between:

 Do what you love. With conviction.  Where discovery lives. And impact drives.  Celebrate difference . Cultivate belonging .  Big thinking. Collectively inspired.  Embrace the journey. Be human. 


 The Opportunity 

NRG is seeking a Research Analyst or Senior Analyst to join our Technology research practice. In this role, you’ll collaborate with some of the world’s most influential brands shaping the future of technology. Our team stays at the forefront of innovation—whether exploring what the next generation of technology might look like, reimagining beloved products, diving deep into the evolving role of AI, and beyond.

In this role, you will support a wide range of initiatives across the full project lifecycle from survey design to report delivery. If you’re passionate about quantitative and qualitative research; if you enjoy visualizing data and discovering insights with confidence; and are looking for a great opportunity to start your career where you can make an impact, this opportunity is for you !

 Your Impact 

 Support all phases of quantitative and qualitative research projects, including research design, questionnaire and discussion guide development, data analysis and storytelling.  Projects may include methods such as concept evaluation, brand studies, content optimization tests, messaging/positioning evaluation, creative materials tests, market sizing and segmentation.  Translate data into clear, actionable insights and recommendations through visual, creative and story-driven reports.  Help drive quality control processes at each step of the research lifecycle, from checking survey programming logic, questionnaire proofing, number checking and proofing reports and presentations for accuracy.  Partner closely with internal teams (programming, fieldwork, data processing, design) to keep projects moving forward on tight timelines.  Leverage AI-enabled approaches to enhance the speed, scale, and depth of insight generation across research and storytelling. 


Who We're Looking For

 Prior Experience – Prior internship or work experience in market research or consumer insights .  Writing and storytelling – You know how to connect the dots and turn complex research findings into clear, compelling narratives. Whether you are writing a report, building a presentation, or presenting to a client, you bring insights to life in a way that captures attention and drives decisions.  Curious and future-minded – You are genuinely interested in seeking information on the “whys,” always digging for more information to understand what makes consumers tick. You’re constantly asking “what’s changing?” and “what’s next?”—especially when it comes to audiences, technology, and content strategy.  Consumer-to-market translator – You’re skilled at moving from consumer insight to strategic implication, helping answer the question: “So what does this mean for our technology clients ?”  Problem Solver – You are a natural problem solver. When something doesn’t go as planned, your first instinct is to look for a solution, rather than viewing it as a roadblock.  Data-driven critical thinker – You’re comfortable working with data to identify trends and insights, including both structured ( i.e. data and hard numbers) and unstructured ( i.e. interviews and qualitative) data. You have experience visualizing data with tools such as Excel and PowerPoint .  Data analysis techniques and software – Familiarity with any of the following data analysis techniques would be ideal: statistical significance testing, correlation analysis, multivariate analysis techniques (such as cluster/segmentation analysis ) and conjoint and discrete choice analysis. Experience with SPSS, Q, or advanced analytics is a plus but not required .  AI-curious and capable – You have experience using AI tools and are thoughtful about how AI can enhance—not replace—insight work.  Self-starter – Internally-motivated who continuously strives to get things done well, regardless of challenges encountered . You are proactive and always keep an eye on the next step.  Clear and proactive communicator – You have excellent verbal communication skills and are able to communicate clearly and succinctly. You’re comfortable asking questions and sharing your point of view.  Hawk-eyed attention to detail – You notice when font sizes change unexpectedly or a proper noun isn’t capitalized. Errors don’t get past you and you are always focused on ensuring high levels of quality control and reporting.  Great team member – T eam player who works collaboratively and harmoniously within a team and across teams. You welcome feedback because you have a zest for learning and growing.  Your degree(s) – You have a B.A./B.S. degree in areas such as Social Sciences, Psychology, Business, Marketing, Market Research, Statistics, Economics or a r elated field. Additional degrees are welcome!

This is a full-time, exempt position.

We embrace the current era of work and what it means to be a best-in-class employer. We understand the flexibility that is required to recruit and retain incredible talent, whether it’s empowering you to do your best work from the comfort of your home or supporting you if you need to take a mental health day for self-care and rest. Below is a unique blend of benefits tailored to meeting the ever-changing professional landscape.

 Flexible/Remote work with optional usage of our great offices in Culver City or New York  Unlimited PTO, volunteer days and a generous number of recharge days including a full office closure during the week of Christmas and New Year’s  Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance Plans  401K with company match  Generous paid Parental Leave  Regular performance evaluations with opportunities for promotions and merit increases  Educational and training reimbursement plan and other training and professional development opportunities  Employee perks program (includes discounts on travel, hotels, cars, fitness, movie tickets and more)  Resources available for mental health, inclusive care and family building  NRGratitude – our company-wide employee recognition program  Regular team/company events and activities including annual summer and holiday parties  Pet friendly headquarters and pet insurance options 


 Our Commitment 

Diversity, equity, and inclusion is at the center of all our practices to ensure that NRG is a place where people from all identities and backgrounds can thrive. NRG is committed to recruiting and retaining diverse talent by supporting their growth through learning programs, internal mobility, affinity group participation and leadership development. rows.descriptionText:
About We Sell Cellular
We Sell Cellular (WSC) is a leading provider in the secondary mobile device industry, specializing in the sourcing, processing, and distribution of pre-owned mobile devices. Through our operations, technology, and industry expertise, we help extend the lifecycle of mobile devices and support a more accessible and sustainable global device ecosystem.
WSC is part of the ITOCHU Group, providing the strength and resources of a global organization while maintaining an entrepreneurial and collaborative working environment. Our team is focused on operational excellence, continued growth, and building a business that delivers long-term value for our customers, employees, and partners.
Position Summary
We Sell Cellular buys used and refurbished mobile devices in volume from carriers, OEM programs, and trade-in channels, and resells them through wholesale and retail channels. Every purchase begins with a bid, and every bid is a pricing judgment: what the device will sell for, what it will cost to grade and refurbish, and what margin remains. This is a developing analytical role designed for an early-career professional who will build expertise in device pricing, purchasing, grading, refurbishment economics, and secondary-market dynamics. The Pricing Analyst will initially work closely with experienced Buyers and the Director of Sourcing and will take on greater ownership of pricing analysis and recommendations as their market knowledge and judgment develop.
This role reports to the Director of Sourcing and supports Buyers and cross-functional teams across Sales, Operations, Finance, and Engineering/Data by analyzing pricing, demand, product condition, and cost data to inform purchasing decisions, monitor margins, and improve pricing accuracy and reporting.
Key Responsibilities
Price Analysis (Purchasing)Market price tracking. Maintain a current view of buy-side and sell-side prices by model, storage, carrier, and grade: daily award prices, secondary-market and wholesale prices, and WSC's own realized sale pricesComparable analysis. Build like-for-like comparisons across sources and time so that a bid can be judged against what the same device actually cost and sold for recentlyMargin visibility. Track the spread between purchase price and realized sale price by category, including grading and refurbishment cost, and flag categories where margin is compressingData hygiene. Keep pricing data sets clean and consistent; flag data quality issues to Engineering / Data rather than working around them
Bid Price Decision SupportBid analysis support. Prepare analysis for lot and program bids, including expected resale value, margin, grade mix, and other key assumptions. Develop pricing recommendations in partnership with Buyers and the Director of Sourcing, taking on greater ownership as market knowledge and experience develop.Scenario analysis. Show how the recommendation changes under different resale prices, grade mixes, or demand conditions, so the Buyer can decide how aggressive to bePricing floor support. Maintain and prepare the data and analysis used by the Director of Sourcing and Buyers to establish and review pricing floors; monitor bids against established parameters and flag exceptions.Post-bid review. Compare bid assumptions with actual outcomes including realized price, grade mix and sell-through and feed the learning back into the next recommendation
Reporting & CommunicationDaily and weekly reporting. Contribute to the daily market report and weekly purchasing KPI review with price movements, margin trends, and notable bidsDocumentation. Record pricing decisions, assumptions, and outcomes so that the team's pricing knowledge accumulates rather than living in individual headsBuyer partnership. Work closely with Buyers on live bids to understand the information needed for purchasing decisions, respond quickly to analytical requests, and progressively build knowledge of WSC's bidding and purchasing process.
QualificationsMust-haveBachelor's degree in business, economics, finance, statistics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experienceStrong numerical judgment and comfort working with prices, margins, and volumes in spreadsheetsAdvanced spreadsheet skills (Google Sheets / Excel): lookups, pivots, scenario tablesClear written communication — able to turn analysis into a one-page recommendation with assumptions and risksMarket curiosity — genuine interest in mobile devices, secondary markets, and how prices moveAttention to detail and ownership of the accuracy of every number handed to a Buyer
PreferredInternship or early-career experience in pricing, purchasing, procurement, finance, merchandising, inventory, supply chain, business analytics, or a related area. Relevant internships, academic projects or equivalent practical experience will be considered. Familiarity with carrier and OEM trade-in programs, device grading, or refurbishment economicsExperience building dashboards or automated reports (Looker Studio, Sheets, or similar)Bilingual (Japanese or Spanish) a plus
Key CompetenciesNumerical judgment — knows when a number looks wrong and checks itDecision support mindset — every analysis ends in a recommendation a Buyer can act onAI adoption — Quick to leverage AI to work faster, with the discipline to double-check all dataMarket awareness — follows device launches, carrier moves, and secondary-market prices as a habitDocumentation discipline — assumptions and outcomes recorded so the team learnsCollaboration — works at the Buyer's pace and in the Buyer's languageLearning orientation — builds device, grading, and market knowledge steadily toward the Buyer track
Working ConditionsThis role is based in Edgewood, NY and requires regular on-site presence to work closely with the Purchasing team and Operations / Grading floor.

Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, technical skills, and other job-related factors.Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including medical insurance, a 401(k)-retirement plan with company match, paid time off (PTO), and paid company holidays.

rows.title: Military SkillBridge Internship - Commercial Banking Credit Analyst

parsed.text: New York City, NY, United States

rows.descriptionText:
We are looking for dedicated and motivated active-duty military veterans to join our team for a Military SkillBridge Internship. This role offers a unique opportunity to leverage your leadership, problem-solving, and analytical skills gained through military service in the fast-paced world of Commercial banking and Credit Analysis. This position is right for you if you have 3-5 years of active duty military leadership experience with a strong preference for combat arms and a passion to start a career in finance and commercial banking.

We offer a full time Military SkillBridge Internship to take you from military service to the finance industry. Our program identifies veterans who have a desire to cut their chops in finance, arms them with an industry-leading financial modeling certification, and places them in finance roles with screened and qualified firms looking for transitioned veterans.

Our certified financial modeling program gives you the skills expected of those entering the financial world on day 1:

Model the three financial statements; Format and color code cells to industry standard; Increase your operating speed in Excel

After passing the financial modeling certification, you will start an internship with a leading reginal commercial bank as a Credit Analyst in training. A commercial banking credit analyst's role involves analyzing financial data, assessing risk, assigning credit scores, preparing reports, and communicating findings to make informed lending decisions that balance the bank's profitability and risk exposure.

Key Responsibilities Of a Credit Analyst

Financial Analysis: Credit analysts evaluate the financial health of businesses by analyzing their financial statements, cash flow, and other relevant data. They assess factors like revenue trends, profit margins, debt levels, and liquidity to determine the borrower's ability to repay loans.Risk Assessment: These analysts assess the risk associated with lending to a particular borrower. They consider industry trends, market conditions, and the borrower's credit history to determine the likelihood of repayment. By identifying potential risks, they help the bank make informed lending decisions.Credit Scoring: Credit analysts use various scoring models to quantify the creditworthiness of applicants. They assign credit scores based on factors such as payment history, credit utilization, and length of credit history. These scores assist in standardizing the evaluation process.Report Preparation: Credit analysts compile their findings into detailed reports that outline their assessment of the applicant's creditworthiness. These reports often include financial ratios, risk analysis, and recommendations for loan terms or credit limits. These reports help senior decision-makers in the bank approve or decline loan applications.Communication: Effective communication is crucial in this role. Credit analysts interact with borrowers to gather additional information, clarify financial details, and discuss potential concerns. They also collaborate with colleagues, such as loan officers and underwriters, to ensure a comprehensive evaluation of each application.

The Ideal Candidate Profile Looks Like

 This position is right for you if you have 3-5 years of active duty military leadership experience (preference for combat arms, but not required) and a passion to start a career in finance and commercial banking. Honorable service and exemplary service evaluations Desire for leadership opportunities in the finance world after you prove your ability to "run through walls" in the short term Willing to virtually attend a no-cost financial modeling certification program and test prior to transition.

**To schedule an intake call with Chamberlain's Veterans' Programs department, simply submit your resume and our team will follow up with you**
